about: betterlink's tour: every step of the first-run flow and of What's New, in one list.
A step never seen shows in What's New after an update. Raise a step's revision (and say what changed) to show it again.
Run `make tour` after editing. `make test` fails when a page, setting, permission or command has no step here. See docs/tour.md.

steps.title: Every link, in the right browser and profile
steps.body: betterlink sits between a click and your browsers. It reads each link you open in any app and sends it to the browser and profile you chose for it. This tour takes about two minutes, and every step can be skipped.

topics.title: Default browser
topics.summary: Links you click come to betterlink first.

steps.title: Make betterlink your default browser
steps.body: macOS sends every link you click to the default browser. Once that is betterlink, it passes each one on to the right profile. macOS asks you to confirm the change.

topics.title: Profiles
topics.summary: The browser profiles links can open in.

steps.title: Find your browser profiles
steps.body: betterlink opens links in the profiles your browsers already have, and reads each browser's list by itself. If a browser shows as not allowed, turn on Full Disk Access for betterlink in Privacy Settings, or add its profiles by hand under Profiles.

topics.title: Fallback profile
topics.summary: Where links that match no rule open.

steps.title: Choose where everything else opens
steps.body: Links that match no rule open in one profile, your fallback. Pick the profile you use most. You can change it any time at the bottom of Link Rules.

topics.title: Link Rules
topics.summary: Send a site to a profile.

steps.title: Send a site to a profile
steps.body: A Link Rule reads "Open domains matching example.com in Work". Rules are checked top to bottom and the first match wins. Add one now, or later under Link Rules, where you can also test any link.
steps.cli: betterlink rules add --kind domain --pattern example.com --profile Work

topics.title: Modifier keys
topics.summary: Hold keys while you click to pick a profile for one link.

steps.title: Hold keys to pick a profile for one click
steps.body: Hold a combination such as ⌃⌘ while you click a link, and it opens in the profile you gave those keys, whatever the rules say. Keep holding until the browser comes forward.

topics.title: See where links go
topics.summary: A toast for each routed link, and a log of every one.

steps.title: A toast says what chose the profile
steps.body: When held keys, config.ts or a Link Rule picks the profile, a small badge names the profile and what chose it, then fades. Links that open in the fallback show none.

steps.title: The Log shows every link, and why
steps.body: Turn on the Log page to see each link, where it went and what sent it there. The log is kept in memory only and cleared when betterlink quits.

topics.title: Always running
topics.summary: The menu bar icon, and opening at login.

steps.title: betterlink lives in the menu bar
steps.body: It has no Dock icon, and closing this window keeps it running and routing links. The menu bar icon opens the window and lists recent links. Hide the icon if you like, and open betterlink from Spotlight instead.

steps.title: Open betterlink at login
steps.body: Start betterlink when you log in, so the first link after a restart opens without a pause and held keys are seen in time. macOS lists it under Login Items.

topics.title: Sidebar
topics.summary: Favorites, folders and live tabs beside your browser window. A preview.

steps.title: A sidebar for your browser
steps.body: betterlink can sit beside a Chromium browser window, Arc style, with Favorites, folders and that window's tabs, in step with the browser both ways. It is a preview, and takes four short steps to set up. Nothing is installed until you do them.

steps.title: Set up the tab helper
steps.body: Set Up writes one small file into the browser's own folder, so the browser can start betterlink's tab helper. Do it for each browser the sidebar should attach to. Uninstall removes the file.

steps.title: Add the Tabs extension
steps.body: The extension tells betterlink about tabs the moment they change. In the browser, open chrome://extensions, turn on Developer mode, then drag the extension's folder from Finder onto the page. Do this once per browser profile, and leave Developer mode on.

steps.title: Let betterlink follow your browser windows
steps.body: The sidebar stays against the browser window as you move and resize it. For that, macOS needs you to allow betterlink under Accessibility. betterlink uses it to follow and resize browser windows and to collapse the browser's own tab strip.
steps.cliWhy: macOS grants Accessibility only in System Settings.

steps.title: Show the sidebar
steps.body: Turn the sidebar on and every browser window of an attached browser gets its own. The shortcut (⌃⌥S unless you change it) hides or shows the sidebar of the browser window in front, and dragging an edge resizes that one. Two windows that look alike show their tabs once clicked. Once on, the Sidebar page shows its other settings.
steps.changed: Every browser window now has its own sidebar, shown while other apps are in front, and the shortcut and a dragged edge change one window's, not all.

steps.title: Favorites, folders and Sidebar Profiles
steps.body: Drag a tab onto the Favorites grid or a folder to save it; it keeps its tab, like a pinned tab in Arc, and a right-click gives a folder an emoji or a symbol. Each Sidebar Profile holds its own Favorites and folders, and the cog at the top picks which one a browser profile shows. Import from Arc or bookmarks on the Sidebar page.
steps.changed: Folders can have an icon now: right-click one and choose an emoji or a built-in symbol, shown in place of the folder.

topics.title: Sync between Macs
topics.summary: Share rules and Sidebar Profiles through a folder your cloud drive syncs.

steps.title: Sync your setup between Macs
steps.body: Pick a folder that Dropbox, Google Drive or iCloud Drive keeps in sync. Each Mac writes its own file there and reads the others', so edits made on two Macs both land. Permissions, and which browser profile shows which Sidebar Profile, stay on each Mac.

topics.title: Agents and the command
topics.summary: Let Claude Code or Codex set up betterlink with its command-line tool.

steps.title: Install the betterlink command
steps.body: Everything this window can change, the betterlink command can change too, so a coding agent can set up your rules for you. Install links it into ~/.local/bin. Then copy the prompt on the Agents page into your agent's chat.
steps.cliWhy: This step installs the command itself.

topics.title: Dia spaces
topics.summary: Open links in the right Dia space.

steps.title: Let betterlink switch Dia's spaces
steps.body: Dia runs as one app and calls its profiles spaces, so betterlink switches Dia to the right space before handing it a link. The first time, macOS asks whether betterlink may control Dia. Without that, Dia links open in your fallback.
steps.cliWhy: macOS asks in its own dialog, and only the app can be the one asking.

topics.title: config.ts
topics.summary: Route with TypeScript when rules aren't enough.

steps.title: Route with TypeScript
steps.body: For anything Link Rules can't express, config.ts is a small function that sees each link, the app it came from and the keys held, and returns a profile. betterlink type-checks it when you save, and keeps the last version that worked.

topics.title: Updates
topics.summary: betterlink checks once a day, and asks before installing.

steps.title: betterlink keeps itself up to date
steps.body: Once a day it asks GitHub whether a newer version is out, and sends nothing about you or your links. It asks before installing. After an update, What's New shows only the steps that are new since you last looked.

steps.title: See what changed in each release
steps.body: The Changelog page lists every release, newest first: the day it shipped and what it changed, each line linked to the pull request behind it. It is built from betterlink's release history, so it never falls behind.

pages.about: Names the app and its licenses, and holds the button that replays this tour.

commands.status: A read-only overview of what the other steps set up.
commands.browsers: A read-only list of installed browsers.
commands.folder: Moving the settings folder is for people who manage their own dotfiles; General explains it, and Sync is the guided way to share settings.
